statement.p: Evaluate the line integral \int_{\mathcal{C}} \mathbf{F} \cdot \,d\ \mathbf{r} where \mathbf{F}=\left\lt -5 \sin x, -5 \cos y, xz \right> and \mathcal{C} is the path given by \mathbf{r}(t) = (3 t^3, 3 t^2, -2 t) for 0 \le t \le 1

static.solution:
\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t)) = \left\lt -5 \sin (3 t^3), -5 \cos (3 t^2), -6 t^4 \right> \mathbf{r} '(t) = \left\lt 9 t^2, 6 t, -2 \right > \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{r} '(t) = \left\lt -5 \sin (3 t^3), -5 \cos (3 t^2), -6 t^4 \right> \cdot \left\lt 9 t^2, 6 t, -2 \right > =-45 t^2 \sin (3 t^3) - 30 t \cos (3 t^2) + 12 t^4
The line integral is then: \int_{\mathcal{C}} \mathbf{F} \cdot \,d\ \mathbf{r} = \int^1_0 \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{r} '(t) \ dt = \int^1_0 -45 t^2 \sin (3 t^3) - 30 t \cos (3 t^2) + 12 t^4\ dt = \left [ 5 \cos (3 t^3) - 5 \sin (3 t^2) + \frac{12}{5} t^5 \right ]^1_0 = 5 \cos (3) - 5 \sin (3) + \frac{-13}{5}
